passage:
Monday: Jagdish kept glancing at the clock in class. His mother had stayed in bed that morning with a fever, and the fractions on the board swam past him. Preeti, his desk-mate, asked what was wrong, and he only shrugged.
Wednesday: He asked his father, "What can I do for Amma?" His father said he could fill her water jug after school and sit with her while she rested. That evening Jagdish also told his teacher, who nodded and said to come to her whenever it felt heavy.
Next Monday: Amma was up making tea. Jagdish still looked at the clock sometimes, but he finished his sums, and Preeti lent him her sharpener.

qa.q: Who sat next to Jagdish in class?
qa.a: Preeti, his desk-mate, sat next to him.

qa.q: Why did Jagdish keep glancing at the clock on Monday?
qa.a: He was worried about his mother, who had stayed in bed with a fever, and probably wanted to know how long until he could go home to her.

qa.q: What helped Jagdish more than worrying alone?
qa.a: Asking his father how he could help gave him small jobs to do, and telling his teacher meant he had another adult who knew. He did not have to make his mother well himself. 🙂

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt when Jagdish shrugged?
qa.a: Preeti may have felt unsure and a little concerned. She noticed something was wrong but did not push, and later she kindly lent him her sharpener.

grounding: A child worries about his unwell mother at school, asks how to help, keeps his routine and tells his teacher.
